rationale: Recorded the account for receipt e68aa5e60d7544c1a620ce12a82f13b8, which completes the vote path with everything produced by the targets themselves: a peer whose snapshot still granted it a vote removed in the committed configuration campaigned on its own, and the peer that had reconstructed no configuration at all answered it, letting a node without a vote in the committed configuration become Leader (comparison 0 violated, valid witness at parsed index 40; the flag-disabled control never campaigned, parsed index 42). Added a fact for that chain, removed the synthesis caveat from the earlier vote fact by pointing it at this receipt, extended the reconstruction fact to the fifth exercised shape, and replaced the question's discriminator with the untested boundaries now that no exercised comparison is left undecided.

investigations.discriminator: No conjecture in this account is now undecided; what would extend or bound it is whether the same divergence arises with a disk-backed commit-tracking store, under crash and restart timing, in repeated or longer windows, or with several divergent instances at once. Those are recorded as limitations rather than as open questions.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across five exercised shapes: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still carried as a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; the demote/promote ladder reported one voter against committed entries of three voters and of five voters; and a peer that had snapshotted itself while still a voter reported three voters after its vote had been removed in the committed configuration, where it holds none. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); the snapshot that supplies the wrong configuration may have been taken by the leader or by the restarting peer itself; no membership change is issued after the restart.
knowledge.changed_premise: Adds the fifth exercised shape observed in receipt e68aa5e60d7544c1a42a1c620ce12a82f13b8, where the snapshot supplying the wrong configuration was taken by the restarting peer itself rather than by a leader, so the divergence also reaches a node that never led a cluster.

knowledge.statement: In the retained vote-path execution the restarted instance acted on support the committed configuration does not sanction: with an empty reconstructed configuration (responder_config_voters 0 against the two voters recorded at index 103 in its own log) it granted a real vote request from a peer that is a member but holds no vote, moving its term from 2 to 3, answering granted true and persisting the vote for that peer at term 3; the same request against the flag-disabled restart of the same instance, which held the configuration entry's own voter count, was refused with granted false and no vote overwritten.
knowledge.conditions: Three-member cluster with one peer demoted to a nonvoter that keeps receiving entries; the responder is restarted alone with no snapshot of its own and is reconnected to the two live peers before the leader is stopped so that it knows no leader; the request carries the demoted peer's real identity, address and last log entry and claims a term one above the responder's. The campaign decision and the term claim of that request were synthesized in this execution; receipt e68aa5e60d7544c1a620ce12a82f13b8 later produced the same grant from a peer campaigning on its own.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier revision described the granted request as delivered on behalf of a peer whose campaign was synthesized. A later receipt produced the same grant without any synthesis, from a peer that campaigned on its own because its reconstruction still granted it a vote, so the caveat now bounds only this earlier execution rather than the finding.

knowledge.statement: In the retained campaign execution a peer that holds no vote in the configuration recorded in its own log acquired leadership on its own initiative: it had snapshotted itself while still a voter (snapshot_config_voters 3), its vote was then removed in the committed configuration (log_config_voters 2, stale_has_vote false), and after both it and the other instance were restarted with the former leader down it reconstructed three voters, campaigned without any external request, and became Leader (campaign_result at parsed index 40: stale_config_voters 3, stale_became_leader true, state Leader) with the other instance — whose own reconstruction held no configuration at all (responder_config_voters 0) — answering one pre-vote and one real vote request from it. The flag-disabled control reconstructed the committed two-voter configuration, held no vote there, sent no request at all and stayed Follower.
knowledge.conditions: Three-member cluster where the campaigning peer took its own snapshot through the public API while still a voter, its vote was then removed by a committed configuration entry, all instances were stopped, and only that peer and one other were restarted with the flag set per case; the former leader stayed down so no known leader could reject the campaign; the restarted peers were reconnected to each other in both directions and the incoming requests were counted by an observer on the answering peer.

interpretations.rationale: Receipt e68aa5e60d7544c1a620ce12a82f13b8 (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed, 43 parsed events) completes the account with a chain in which every action is produced by the targets themselves. Comparison 0 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 40: the peer that had snapshotted itself while still a voter reconstructed three voters, campaigned on its own after its vote had been removed in the committed configuration (campaign_inputs at parsed index 39: log_config_voters 2 with the peer holding no vote, snapshot_config_voters 3, tracked commit index 23 covering that entry), and became Leader while holding no vote in its own log's committed configuration; comparison 2 holds at the same index, recording that its real vote request reached the other instance, which had reconstructed no configuration at all, and comparison 1 holds at parsed index 42, where the flag-disabled control reconstructed the committed two-voter configuration, held no vote, sent nothing and stayed Follower. This removes the synthesis caveat that the earlier vote-path receipt carried: the campaign, the requests and the grant are all real, and the only reason the peer could campaign was the reconstructed configuration. The current account, each result under its own receipt, is: NewRaft's configuration scan starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) and restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the tracked commit index first, so a committed configuration entry inside that prefix is never re-derived [scan_start, restore_lastapplied, cfg_entry]; the reconstruction then differs from the node's own log in both directions and across five exercised shapes, whether the wrong configuration comes from a leader's snapshot or the peer's own (receipts 63d4401225884bdd9c75fbe580336c63, faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1, c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce, 29f7b510513642f499f8646cb55dccfe, e68aa5e60d7544c1a620ce12a82f13b8), and it persists under a live healthy leader until a configuration entry is appended (a1c98fc2bafd4775aa05275dd25f2767). That context then: leaves a sole committed member unable to campaign or contending for a quorum it can never reach; lets a node take leadership and commit with support from a minority of the committed configuration; ends with a client-acknowledged commit either resting on one copy or, when a majority that never held it forms higher-term leadership, discarded from every store; grants and durably records a vote for a peer that holds no vote; and lets a peer that holds no vote acquire leadership with the help of a node that holds no configuration at all (this receipt). No exercised comparison is left undecided; the boundaries that remain are the recorded limitations.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces these effects: excluded wherever tested, by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same requests and decisions.

The discard required an extra legal election to put the successor leadership in a strictly higher term, and the campaign required the former leader to be down: with the successor in the same term as the stale holder the acknowledged copy survived on the holder (receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce), and a live leader would have refused support through its known-leader rejection. The consequences therefore hold under stated conditions rather than unconditionally.

In every case the returning or answering peers were rebuilt with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled unless the case was about their own divergence, and membership ladders were built from demote/promote or remove; the exercised question is what a divergent node's context does in a cluster of otherwise correct nodes.
limitations: Single process with in-memory transports and in-memory commit-tracking stores, no crash injection, no disk-backed store and no network fault model.

The exercises restart one or two instances at a time and use single-shot windows (200-1500 ms depending on the case, 3000 ms for leadership, 1000-1500 ms for commits); no rate, repetition or long-run stability claim follows.

The earlier delivered-request vote case carries a synthesized campaign and term claim; the self-produced campaign receipt supersedes it as evidence for the same grant, and pre-vote-only campaigns were not exercised in isolation.
Reconstruction shapes beyond the five exercised ones, other stores and other flags were not varied.
